title: Yu-Gi-Oh!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Bullied, game-loving Yugi Mutou solves the ancient Egyptian Millennium Puzzle and becomes host to the spirit of a nameless pharaoh. When Yugi or his friends are threatened, the spirit challenges wrongdoers to Shadow Games whose losers suffer supernatural Penalty Games. Later arcs center on the card game Duel Monsters as Yugi and his friends help the pharaoh recover his lost memories.
life_message: Friendship, courage and fair play matter more than winning, and wrongdoers face what they deserve.

content.note: Early chapters' Penalty Games inflict burns, madness and worse on villains; later deadly duels (Wikipedia: 'unexpectedly dark'; AniList Death Game 69, Torture 40, Gore 25).
Possession, soul-stealing and dark Egyptian magic (AniList Body Horror, Dissociative Identities; MangaUpdates Game of Death).
Mild crushes and a few lecherous gags (MangaUpdates Perverted Character/s).
Bullying of Yugi early on; split identity with the pharaoh (AniList Bullying 58).
High-stakes gambling and wagering games (AniList Gambling 71).
The story fed a card game franchise with billions of cards sold (Wikipedia reception; AniList Card Battle 88).

dominant: Friendship; games as moral trials; Egyptian occult mythology

frames.aligns: Friendship, loyalty and fairness win; bullies and cheats are exposed.
frames.concerns: Occult possession, Egyptian gods and dark magic presented as real power.
Possession by a spirit, dark rituals and idol imagery.
Spirit possession, gambling, occult items and gods.
Possession, curses and summoned monsters central.
Pagan gods and occult power; gambling.
Retributive punishments; sexism noted by MangaUpdates (to verify).
Gambling, idols, Egyptian gods and sorcery.

frames.aligns: Karma-like justice through Penalty Games; dharma of friendship.
Courage, loyalty and honor in contests.

frames.concerns: Spiritism, magic, violence and gambling all central.

frames.aligns: Mythology and ancient gods treated with awe.

frames.concerns: Egyptian rather than Japanese spirits; violence.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Every insult or cheat is answered with a game and a penalty.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Yugi and friends act on their own, outside school authority.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friendship bonds rather than family drive the story.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Pharaoh's royal past matters; friends relate as equals.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Ancient magic and fate shape events.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in deadly games balanced with fun and friendship.

folkways.japan: Group friendship (nakama), the school setting and game culture reflect Japanese youth culture of the 1990s.

delivery.evidence: Friendship and fair play carried by duels and Penalty Games; no review on delivery found (to verify).
delivery.note: Wrongdoers are punished in games, and friendship is carried by the plot, per summaries.

winners_losers: Yugi and his friends win; cheats and bullies suffer penalties. Loyal friendship gets sympathy.
